title: Full beat-by-beat script: overnight SSH triage on jump01 (Terminal.app + Google Sheets + Google Docs in Firefox)

steps.title: Opener
steps.window: The recorder card, then the Goal doc (Firefox)
steps.do: Read the opener off the recorder card, cursor still, with no pause after "in mind". During the last words start sliding the cursor toward the yellow minimise button of the Goal doc, then minimise the recorder. Keep the cursor sliding up and left from the Goal doc text toward the yellow minimise button at the top left of its window while you speak, with no pause after "blocked". Click the yellow minimise button at the top left of the Goal doc window, on the word "Minimising", and narrate the rest as it happens.
say: "Step 1: I will be beginning my task soon. Here is the workflow I have in mind."
"I'm going through last night's failed SSH logins on jump01, to decide what gets blocked."
"Minimising the Goal doc: my cursor's on the yellow button, top left of its window, and I left click it, to clear the screen."

steps.title: Terminal first look
steps.window: Dock, then the Terminal window
steps.do: Move the cursor down to the Dock on the left edge, onto the Terminal icon, and click it to bring Terminal forward (it is already open in Documents/Project). Pause 1 s after "I click it". Look at the Terminal window: the "$ " prompt in Documents/Project, 16 pt. Type wc -l auth-jump01.log at the prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the output line: 59 auth-jump01.log. Hold on to 59 for the import check.
say: "Step 2: okay, Terminal first. Down to the Dock on the left edge, onto the Terminal icon, and I click it, since it's already open in Project."
"Alright, Terminal's up, with the prompt in Documents, Project."
"Typing w c, space, dash l, then auth-jump01.log, a raw line count to check the import against, and Return."
"59 lines in auth-jump01.log, so that's my import check."

steps.title: Count failed and unknown-account logins
steps.window: Terminal window
steps.do: Type grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log at the prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the count on the next line: 53. Type grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log on the next prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the count on the next line: 14. Rest the cursor on the two counts, 53 and 14, and say what they mean for the pivot check.
steps.type:
grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log
grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log
say: "Step 3: the failures. Typing grep dash c, Failed password in quotes, and the log name, then Return, for a number to hit."
"It says 53, so that's 53 Failed password lines to match."
"Same again, but invalid user in quotes, then Return, to count tries on accounts that don't exist."
"14 invalid user lines, so someone's guessing usernames, not just fumbling a password."
"So both counts are my bar: if the pivot isn't 53, the import's wrong, and I'd recheck."

steps.title: List successful logins
steps.window: Terminal window
steps.do: Type grep 'Accepted' auth-jump01.log (Accepted in single quotes) while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the six Accepted lines: publickey at 00:30:00, 07:05:00 and 07:40:00; password at 03:52:34 for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77, 04:20:34 for jsmith from 198.51.100.140 and 06:04:12 for ops.admin from 10.20.4.11. Rest the cursor on line 2: 03:52:34, Accepted password for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77, port 62963, and say you will come back to it. Look over the password lines and say why those IPs are compared in the sheet rather than blocked from Terminal.
say: "Step 4: who got in. Typing grep, Accepted in single quotes, the log name, and Return, to list every login."
"Six Accepted lines, three publickey and three password, and the password ones are my focus."
"Second line, 03:52:34, Accepted password for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77. Hmm, I'll come back to that."
"An IP that failed, then got in, needs its account checked, so I'll compare those in the sheet first."

steps.title: Leave Terminal for the sheet
steps.window: Terminal window, Dock, then Google Sheets (Firefox)
steps.do: Move up to the top left of the Terminal window and click the yellow minimise button. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Move down the Dock on the left to the minimised sheets window and click it to bring the sheet back. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Read Google Sheets in Firefox: the title "jump01 overnight triage" at the top and an empty grid under it.
say: "Step 5: Terminal's done for now. Up to the yellow minimise button, top left of its window, and a left click hides it."
"Down the Dock on the left, to the minimised sheets window, and I click it to bring the sheet back."
"Google Sheets is up, titled jump01 overnight triage, with an empty grid."

steps.title: Import the log export and check it
steps.window: Google Sheets (Firefox) > Import files dialog > Mac file picker
steps.do: Move up to the Sheets menu bar, to File on the far left, and left click it. Pause 1 s after "left click it". Move down the File menu to Import and select it. Pause 1 s after "select it". In the Import files box click the Upload tab along the top (the file is on the Mac, not in Drive). Pause 1 s after "click the Upload tab". Click Browse in the middle of the Upload tab. Pause 1 s after "I press it". In the Mac file picker click Documents once in the left sidebar. Pause 1 s after "one click". Double-click Project in the list on the right. Pause 1 s after "double-click it". Click auth-jump01-excerpt.csv once to select it; say "excerpt", not the extension. Pause 1 s after "selects it". Click Open at the bottom right of the picker. Pause 1 s after "a click". In the Import file box, under Import location, click Replace current sheet. Pause 1 s after "I pick it". Click Import data at the bottom of the box. Pause 1 s after "I press it". Wait while the rows fill in, staying silent for up to 4 s. Read row 1: timestamp, host, event, user, invalid_user, src_ip, decision. src_ip is column F, the filter column. Look over at column G, decision: it is empty all the way down. Hold Command and press Down to jump to the bottom of the data, while speaking, with no pause. Read the last row number on the left: 60, timestamp 07:40:00. Check: 60 minus the header row is 59, and Terminal said 59 lines. They match, so the import dropped nothing. Hold Command and press Up to return to the top row, while speaking, with no pause.
say: "Step 6: getting the export in. Up to the Sheets menu bar, File on the far left, and I left click it, since File holds Import."
"Down the list to Import, and I select it, to bring data into this sheet."
"An Import files box opens. The file's on my Mac, so I click the Upload tab."
"Middle of the tab, Browse, and I press it to pick the file myself."
"The Mac file picker's open. Documents in the left sidebar, and one click picks it, since the inputs sit under it."
"Project's in the list on the right, since it holds both inputs, and I double-click it."
"Inside Project, the excerpt file, a spreadsheet copy of the same 59 lines, so one click selects it."
"Bottom right of the picker, Open, and a click to start the upload."
"Under Import location, Replace current sheet, and I pick it, because this blank one's already named for the job."
"Bottom of the box, Import data, and I press it to bring the rows in."
"Waiting a second while the rows fill in."
"Checking the import. Row 1 reads timestamp, host, event, user, invalid user, src ip and decision, so src ip is column F, my filter column."
"Over in column G, decision, it's empty all the way down, and I'll fill that in myself."
"Holding Command and pressing Down to the bottom, and the last row number on the left is 60, timestamped 07:40:00."
"Sixty minus the header is 59, and Terminal said 59 lines. They match, so the import dropped nothing."
"Command and Up, back to the top row."

steps.title: Freeze the header and add a filter
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1
steps.do: Move up to View in the Sheets menu bar and left click it. Pause 1 s after "left click it". Move down to Freeze; a submenu slides out to the right. Pause 1 s after "Freeze". Move across into the submenu and select 1 row. Pause 1 s after "I select it". Go up to the toolbar, right side, onto the Create a filter icon (its tooltip shows) and click it. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Read row 1: a filter icon in every header, A1 to G1.
say: "Step 7: freezing the header before I scroll. Up to View in the menu bar, and I left click it, since freeze lives there."
"Freeze is next, so a menu slides out on the right."
"Across to 1 row, and I select it, so the column names stay up top."
"Toolbar, on the right, the Create a filter icon, its tooltip showing, and I click it, to filter by IP later."
"Row 1 has a filter icon in every header, A1 to G1, so the filter's on."

steps.title: Insert the pivot table
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 > Create pivot table dialog
steps.do: Move down from the filter icons onto cell A1 and click it. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Press Command A while speaking, with no pause, then read the name box at the top left: A1:G60. Move up to Insert in the Sheets menu bar and open it. Pause 1 s after "I open it". Move down the Insert menu to Pivot table and choose it with a left click. Pause 1 s after "choose it". In the Create pivot table box, click New sheet. Pause 1 s after "I pick it". Click Create at the bottom right of the box. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Read the bottom tabs: a new tab, Pivot Table 1, with the editor open on the right. Think aloud: COUNTIF would mean a formula per IP and event pair; a pivot counts them all at once.
say: "Step 8: the pivot. Down from the filter icons onto A1, and I click it, to start the selection."
"Command A selects everything, and the name box at the top left says A1 to G60."
"Up to Insert in the menu bar, and I open it, since the pivot option lives there."
"Then Pivot table, and I choose it with a left click, to get one row per IP."
"In the Create pivot table box, New sheet, and I pick it, so Sheet1's rows stay untouched."
"Bottom right of the box, Create, and a left click, to give the pivot its own tab."
"A new tab at the bottom, Pivot Table 1, with the editor open on the right."
"Let me think. COUNTIF means a formula per pair, and a pivot counts them all at once, so pivot."

steps.title: Build the pivot: rows, columns, values
steps.window: Google Sheets: Pivot Table 1, pivot editor
steps.do: In the editor on the right, click the Add button beside Rows. Pause 1 s after "and I click". In the list that drops down, move to src_ip and click it. Pause 1 s after "click it". Move further down to Columns and left click its Add button. Pause 1 s after "a left click". In the list, select event. Pause 1 s after "select it". On the Columns card, click the Show totals checkbox to untick it. Pause 1 s after "with a click". Read across row 2 of the pivot: B Accepted password, C Accepted publickey, D Failed password. Move down to Values and click its Add button. Pause 1 s after "and I click". In the list that opens, pick event. Pause 1 s after "pick event". Look lower on the value card at the Summarize by box to see what it is set to. If it says COUNTA go to the next line; if it says SUM, skip to the line after. If it already shows COUNTA, leave it as it is. Only if it shows SUM: click the Summarize by dropdown, move down to COUNTA and click it. Pause 1 s after "COUNTA and click it". Say why COUNTA fits: each line is one attempt, and it counts the text entries. Read the grid on the left: the counts fill in, with a Grand Total on row 9.
say: "Step 9: the rows. In the editor on the right, the Add button beside Rows, and I click, so IPs go down the side."
"A list drops down, so I move to src underscore ip and click it, for a row per address."
"Further down, Columns, its Add button, and a left click, to put event types across the top."
"From the list, event, and I select it, since that's each try's type."
"Under that, Show totals is ticked, and I untick it with a click, since I only need counts per event."
"Row 2 across: B Accepted password, C Accepted publickey, D Failed password."
"Down to Values, its Add button, and I click, to say what's counted."
"In the list, I pick event, since every row has one."
"Lower on the value card, the Summarize by box, to see what it's set to."
"It shows COUNTA already, so I leave it."
"If it shows SUM, I click that dropdown, move to COUNTA and click it, since these are words."
"Each line's one attempt, so COUNTA fits, since it counts the text entries."
"The counts fill in on the left, with a Grand Total on row 9."

steps.title: Sort, check the total and read the ranking
steps.window: Google Sheets: Pivot Table 1, pivot editor
steps.do: Go back up to the Rows card, open Order and choose Descending. Pause 1 s after "choose Descending". Under it, on the same card, click the Sort by dropdown and pick Failed password. Pause 1 s after "pick Failed password". Read down rows 3 to 8: 203.0.113.45 18, 198.51.100.23 14, 192.0.2.77 9, 198.51.100.140 7, 10.20.4.11 3 (say it as the ten-dot address), 192.0.2.200 2. Look at columns B and C, rows 5 to 7: 192.0.2.77 and 198.51.100.140 have 1 in B; the ten-dot address has 1 in B and 3 in C. Say that sorted this way you work down from the biggest risk. Click the close icon at the top right of the editor. Pause 1 s after "a click closes it". Move down to the bottom of column D and click D9. Pause 1 s after "a click selects it". Check: D9 reads 53 and grep said 53 in Terminal. They match, so nothing is missing. Look just left of D9: B9 and C9 are 3 each, password and publickey, the same as Terminal.
say: "Step 10: noisiest first. Up to the Rows card, Order, and I open it and choose Descending, for big numbers first."
"Below that, Sort by, and I click the dropdown and pick Failed password, so the most failures sit on top."
"In column B, 192.0.2.77 and 198.51.100.140 each got in once after failing, and the ten-dot address has 1 in B, 3 in C."
"So, sorted like this, I'll work down from the biggest risk."
"Top right of the editor, the close icon, and a click closes it, to get the full sheet back."
"Down to the bottom of column D, D9, and a click selects it, to read the failure total."
"D9 reads 53, and grep said 53 in Terminal. They match, so nothing's missing."
"Just left of it, B9 and C9 are 3 each, password and publickey, same as Terminal."

steps.title: Decision column and dropdown chips
steps.window: Google Sheets: Pivot Table 1 > Data validation panel
steps.do: Move right of the pivot to cell E2 and click it. Pause 1 s after "click it". Type Decision in E2 while speaking, with no pause, then press Return to drop to E3. Click E3, beside 203.0.113.45. Pause 1 s after "I select it". Hold Shift and press Down five times, while speaking, with no pause. Read the name box: E3:E8. Move up to Insert in the Sheets menu bar and open it. Pause 1 s after "I open it". Choose Dropdown from the Insert menu. Pause 1 s after "I select it". The Data validation panel opens on the right. Click into the Option 1 box and type Block while speaking, with no pause. Click Add another item under it. Pause 1 s after "I hit it". In the Option 2 box underneath, type Watch while speaking, with no pause. Click Add another item again, lower down. Pause 1 s after "I press it". In the Option 3 box, type Ignore while speaking, with no pause. Click Done at the bottom of the panel to save. Pause 1 s after "a click saves it". Read E3 to E8: each shows a dropdown chip now.
say: "Step 11: a decision column. Right of the pivot, E2, and I click it, so decisions sit beside the counts."
"Typing Decision, so it's clear what the column's for, then Return to drop to E3."
"Down to E3, beside 203.0.113.45, and I select it, since the range starts on the first IP."
"Shift and Down five times, and the name box says E3 to E8."
"Up to Insert in the menu bar, and I open it, since Dropdown's in that menu."
"Then Dropdown, and I select it, to force fixed words."
"A Data validation panel opens on the right. I'm clicking into the Option 1 box to type Block."
"Below, Add another item, and I hit it, to make a second box."
"In Option 2 underneath, typing Watch, since that's the middle ground."
"Lower down, Add another item again, and I press it, to make a third box."
"In Option 3, typing Ignore, so harmless addresses have a word."
"Down to Done at the bottom of the panel, and a click saves it."
"Fixed words, because COUNTIF needs exact matches, and E3 to E8 each show a chip now."

steps.title: Filter, read and mark 203.0.113.45
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 filter, then Pivot Table 1
steps.do: Move down to the sheet tabs at the bottom left and click Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "I click Sheet1". Go up to F1 and click its filter icon at the right edge of the cell. Pause 1 s after "I click its filter icon". In the filter panel, under Filter by values, press Clear. Pause 1 s after "I press Clear". Scroll down the value list to 203.0.113.45 and tick it. Pause 1 s after "I tick it". Click OK at the bottom right of the panel. Pause 1 s after "left click it". Read the count in the bottom right of the window: 18 rows, every one a Failed password. Read columns D, E and A: root and admin, no on every row of column E, 01:12:00 to 01:16:05, and no Accepted line. Say your verdict for 203.0.113.45 from the rows: 18 failures, root 11 and admin 7, no Accepted line, so Block. Move down to the tabs and click Pivot Table 1, to the right of Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Go to E3, next to 203.0.113.45, and click its chip. Pause 1 s after "I click its chip". In the list under the chip, pick Block. Pause 1 s after "pick Block". Read E3: it now shows Block.
say: "Step 12: raw rows for the top IP first. Down to the tabs at the bottom left, and I click Sheet1."
"Up to F1, and I click its filter icon, since src_ip is my filter column."
"Under Filter by values, I press Clear, so nothing's ticked."
"Down the list to 203.0.113.45, and I tick it, so only its rows come back."
"Bottom right of the panel, OK, and I left click it, to apply the filter."
"Okay, just this IP, 18 rows, every one a Failed password."
"Column D is root and admin, column E says no on every row, 01:12:00 to 01:16:05, and nothing's Accepted."
"18 failures, root 11, admin 7, no Accepted line: real admin names from outside, never in. So this one's a Block."
"Over to Pivot Table 1, right of Sheet1, and a left click, so the decision goes beside the count."
"Over to E3, next to 203.0.113.45, and I click its chip."
"In the list, I pick Block, to match what I said."
"So E3 now shows Block."

steps.title: Filter, read and mark the other three IPs
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 filter, then Pivot Table 1
steps.do: Move down to the sheet tabs at the bottom left and click Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Go up to F1 and click its filter icon. Pause 1 s after "I click its filter icon". In the filter panel, under Filter by values, press Clear first. Pause 1 s after "I press Clear". Down the value list tick 198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.140 and 192.0.2.200, so only these three stay. Pause 1 s after "only these three stay". Click OK at the bottom right of the panel. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Read the count in the bottom right: 24 rows, 14 for 198.51.100.23, 8 for 198.51.100.140 and 2 for 192.0.2.200. Read the first rows, for 198.51.100.23: test, ubuntu and oracle, all invalid users, 02:03:00 to 02:05:23, nothing Accepted. Say your verdict: Block. Read the middle rows, for 198.51.100.140: jsmith fails 7 times from 04:15:00 to 04:18:08, then Accepted password at 04:20:34. Say your verdict: Watch. Read the last rows, for 192.0.2.200: root twice, 05:30:00 and 05:31:00, no login. Say your verdict: Ignore. Move down to the tabs and click Pivot Table 1. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Go to E4, beside 198.51.100.23, and click its chip. Pause 1 s after "I click its chip". In the list, pick Block. Pause 1 s after "pick Block". Two rows down, click the E6 chip beside 198.51.100.140 and pick Watch. Pause 1 s after "pick Watch". Two rows further down, click the E8 chip beside 192.0.2.200 and pick Ignore. Pause 1 s after "pick Ignore". Read E4, E6 and E8: each shows its word, and E3 above keeps its own.
say: "Step 13: the other three together. Down to Sheet1 at the bottom left, and I click it."
"Up to F1, and I click its filter icon."
"In the panel, Filter by values, I press Clear first, to start empty."
"Then ticking 198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.140 and 192.0.2.200 down the list, so only these three stay."
"OK at the bottom right, and I click it, to apply the filter."
"198.51.100.23: 14 failures, test, ubuntu and oracle, all invalid users, 02:03:00 to 02:05:23, nothing Accepted. A Block."
"198.51.100.140: jsmith fails 7 times, 04:15:00 to 04:18:08, then gets in at 04:20:34. Could be a guessed password, so Watch."
"192.0.2.200: root twice, 05:30:00 and 05:31:00, no login. Just 2 tries, so Ignore."
"Pivot Table 1 next, and a left click, to record these beside their counts."
"Over to E4, beside 198.51.100.23, and I click its chip."
"From the list, I pick Block, since no login came."
"Two rows down, E6, beside 198.51.100.140, I click its chip and pick Watch, since it got in."
"Two more down, E8, beside 192.0.2.200, I click its chip and pick Ignore, since it's only two tries."
"E4, E6 and E8 have their words now, and E3 above still keeps its own."

steps.title: Filter, read and mark 192.0.2.77
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 filter, then Pivot Table 1
steps.do: Move down to the sheet tabs at the bottom left and click Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Go back up to F1 and left click its filter icon. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Under Filter by values, press Clear so no old ticks remain. Pause 1 s after "I press Clear". Scroll down the value list to 192.0.2.77 and tick it. Pause 1 s after "I tick it". Click OK at the bottom right of the panel. Pause 1 s after "left click it". Read the count in the bottom right: 10 rows, 9 failures and one Accepted line near the end. Read down the rows: svc_backup and deploy fail from 03:40:00 to 03:45:49, then svc_backup gets in with Accepted password at 03:52:34. Say your verdict for 192.0.2.77: nine failures, seven on svc_backup, last at 03:45:49, in at 03:52:34, six minutes forty-five seconds later. Watch. Move down to the tabs and click Pivot Table 1. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Go to E5, next to 192.0.2.77, and click its chip. Pause 1 s after "I click its chip". In the list, pick Watch. Pause 1 s after "pick Watch". Read E5: its chip shows Watch.
say: "Step 14: the third IP by rank, 192.0.2.77. Down to Sheet1 at the bottom left, and I click it."
"Back up to F1's filter icon, and a left click opens it."
"Again under Filter by values, I press Clear, so no old ticks remain."
"Down the list to 192.0.2.77, and I tick it, so only its rows stay."
"OK at the bottom right, and I left click it, to apply the filter."
"Okay, just this IP, 10 rows: 9 failures and one Accepted line near the end."
"Reading down the rows, svc_backup and deploy fail from 03:40:00 to 03:45:49, then svc_backup gets in with Accepted password at 03:52:34."
"Nine failures, seven on svc_backup, last at 03:45:49. svc_backup's in at 03:52:34, six minutes forty-five seconds later. A guess, or the backup? Watch."
"Back on Pivot Table 1 with a left click, so this one gets marked too."
"Over to E5, next to 192.0.2.77, and I click its chip."
"I pick Watch, because that's what the rows point to."
"E5's chip shows Watch now."

steps.title: Filter, read and mark 10.20.4.11
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 filter, then Pivot Table 1
steps.do: Move down to the sheet tabs at the bottom left and left click Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "left click it". Go up to F1 and click its filter icon. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Under Filter by values, press Clear. Pause 1 s after "I press Clear". Near the top of the value list, tick 10.20.4.11 (say it as the ten-dot address). Pause 1 s after "tick it". Click OK at the bottom right of the panel. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Read the count in the bottom right: 7 rows, with a publickey login at 00:30:00, then failures, then Accepted logins. Read across the rows: ops.admin fails three times, 06:02:00 to 06:02:51, then gets in at 06:04:12, plus publickey logins at 00:30:00, 07:05:00 and 07:40:00. Say your verdict for 10.20.4.11: internal, a known admin, a login right after, only three fails. Ignore. Move down to the tabs and click Pivot Table 1. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Go to E7, beside the ten-dot address, and click its chip. Pause 1 s after "I click its chip". In the list, pick Ignore. Pause 1 s after "pick Ignore". Read E7: it shows Ignore.
say: "Step 15: the internal address. Down to Sheet1 at the bottom left, and I left click it."
"Up to F1's filter icon, and I click it."
"Filter by values, and I press Clear, so the old tick goes."
"The ten-dot address is near the top, so I tick it, to have it alone."
"Then OK, bottom right, and a left click, to apply it."
"Right, seven rows now: a publickey login at 00:30:00, then failures, then Accepted logins."
"Reading across, it's a private ten-dot address. ops.admin fails three times, 06:02:00 to 06:02:51, then gets in at 06:04:12, plus publickey logins."
"Internal, a known admin, a login right after, only three fails, and publickey logins either side. That's a mistyped password, so Ignore."
"Pivot Table 1 again, and a left click, so I can mark it."
"Over to E7, beside the ten-dot address, and I click its chip."
"I pick Ignore, because that's what fits these rows."
"E7 shows Ignore now."

steps.title: Clear the filter and total the decisions
steps.window: Google Sheets: Sheet1 filter, then Pivot Table 1
steps.do: Move down to the sheet tabs at the bottom left and click Sheet1. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Go up to F1 and click its filter icon to open the value list. Pause 1 s after "I click it". In the panel click Select all, so all 59 rows come back. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Click OK at the bottom right of the panel, then read the left edge: row 60 is back. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Move down to the tabs and switch to Pivot Table 1. Pause 1 s after "I switch to it". Click D10, just under the pivot. Pause 1 s after "a click there". Type Block, Return, Watch, Return, Ignore, Return down D10 to D12, while speaking, with no pause. Move one cell right to E10, beside Block, and click it. Pause 1 s after "I click it". Type =COUNTIF(E3:E8,"Block") in E10 while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. In E11 type =COUNTIF(E3:E8,"Watch") and press Return, then in E12 type =COUNTIF(E3:E8,"Ignore") and press Return, while speaking, with no pause. Read E10 to E12: Block 2, Watch 2, Ignore 2. Check they add up to the six IPs in E3 to E8.
say: "Step 16: every row back first. Down to Sheet1, bottom left, and I click it, to clear the filter."
"F1's filter icon again, and I click it, to open the value list."
"Select all in the panel, and I click it, so all 59 rows come back."
"OK at the bottom right, and I click it. Row 60's back on the left, so the full data's there."
"Down to Pivot Table 1, and I switch to it, because the totals go under the pivot."
"D10, under the pivot, and a click there, so the totals sit under the decisions."
"Typing Block, Watch and Ignore down D10 to D12, pressing Return after each, as labels."

"From the raw log, so an import slip would show: failures 18, 14, 9, 7, 3, 2 match D3 to D8, and logins 4, 1, 1 match B and C."
